translation: The Verse Summary of Perfect Wisdom
The Verse Summary of Perfect Wisdom
Prologue
In the language of India: Arya-prajnaparamita-sancayagatha. In the language of Tibet: The Noble Verse Summary of Perfect Wisdom. We bow to Noble Manjushri!
Then, to bring great joy to the four assemblies, the Blessed One taught perfect wisdom again. At that time, he spoke these verses.

Feel great joy, respect, and trust. Clear away blocks and mental troubles to go beyond stains. Listen to the perfect wisdom of the gentle ones who work for the good of beings. This is where the heroes practice their way of living.

A wandering seeker named Shrenika used his knowledge to destroy the heaps that no one can grasp. An awakening hero understands things in this exact same way. They do not touch the peace beyond sorrow. Instead, they stay right there in wisdom.

They also ask, "What is this wisdom? Whose is it? Where does it come from?" They see that all these things are empty. They look at them closely without feeling sad or afraid. That awakening hero is close to awakening.

Some do not truly understand. They see form. They focus on the heaps of feeling, intention, and awareness. They might even think, "These heaps are empty." But that awakening hero is still practicing with signs. They lack faith in the state that is never born.

Others do not practice in form, feeling, idea, or intention. They do not practice in awareness. They practice without staying anywhere. They do not grasp at what is called "practicing." Instead, they rely on wisdom. With a mind that knows what is never born, they touch the highest, peaceful deep calm.

Any awakening hero who stays here like this is completely at peace. The Thus-Gone Ones of the past have given a prediction about them. They are not proud. They never think, "I am resting in calm," or "I have stood up." Why? Because they fully understand the nature of things.

By practicing like this, they practice the wisdom of the Well-Gone Ones. They truly understand that not practicing is the real practice. They do not grasp at any of the things they practice. This is the practice of the highest perfect wisdom.
Teaching About Knowing Everything in Every Way

Chapter one: Teaching about knowing everything in every way. Many rivers flow here in Jambudvipa. They make flowers, fruits, healing plants, and forests grow. They all depend on the serpent king. This is the lord of the serpent spirits who lives in Anavatapta. All this growth comes from the great power of that lord of the serpent spirits.

Whatever teaching the listeners of the Victorious One share, they explain it clearly with good reasons. Their words bring great joy and good results. All of this comes from the power of the Thus-Gone One.

Why is this? Because the Victorious One has shared many ways of teaching. His students practice these ways completely. After they master them, they teach exactly what they practiced. They do this by the power of the Buddha, not by their own strength.

An awakening hero does not hold onto perfect wisdom. They do not hold onto an awakening hero or the wish to awaken. When they hear this, they are not confused or afraid. That awakening hero practices the wisdom of the Well-Gone Ones.

There is no form, no feeling, no idea, and no intention. For that person, awareness does not have even a tiny speck of a place to rest. They do not rest on any things. They practice without resting anywhere. Without grasping, they reach the awakening of the Well-Gone Ones.

What does not exist is called non-existent. Unwise people imagine this. They think that things exist or do not exist. But existing and not existing are not real things. Any awakening hero who knows this will surely break free.

Someone here knows the five heaps are like an illusion. They do not treat the illusion as one thing and the five heaps as another. They are free from any different idea and practice in perfect peace. This is the practice of the highest perfect wisdom.

Someone with a wise friend and clear insight will never be afraid. They will not be scared to hear the Mother of the Victorious Ones. But someone with a bad friend just relies on others. They are like an unbaked clay pot that falls apart when touched by water.

You might ask, "Why is this person called an awakening hero?" They cut off clinging. They want to completely end clinging to everything. They touch the awakening of a Victorious One, which is a state of not clinging. Because of this, they get the name awakening hero.

You might ask, "Why is this person called a great hero?" It is because they become the highest in the large crowd of living beings. They cut through the strong, wrong views in the realm of living beings. That is why they are called a great hero.

They have great giving, great intelligence, and great power. They have entered the highest Great Vehicle of the Victorious Ones. They put on the great armor and defeat the tricks of Mara. For these reasons, they are called a great hero.

Someone might hold the idea of living beings and the idea of suffering. They might think, "I will help beings and end their suffering." That makes them an awakening hero who only imagines a self and living beings. This is not the practice of highest perfect wisdom.

You should know that all living beings are just like the self. Know that all things are just like all living beings. Do not think about arising or no arising. This is the practice of highest perfect wisdom.

People in the world have many names for things. But you must let go of their arising and passing away. Then you will gain the highest, deathless deep knowing. There is nothing greater than this. That is why it is called perfect wisdom.

Any awakening hero who practices this way without doubt has true wisdom. You should know they rest in sameness. They completely understand that all things are with no nature of their own. This is the practice of highest perfect wisdom.
The second chapter, teaching knowing all the paths.
Teaching knowing all the paths.

Imagine a magician creates a fake crowd at a crossroads and then cuts off all their heads. The awakening hero knows that all beings are just like those illusions. Because they know this, the awakening hero has no fear.

Form, idea, feeling, intention, and awareness are not tied up or set free. They do not truly exist. You must enter into awakening this way without losing heart. This is the best armor for holy persons.

Why is this called the Great Vehicle of Awakening? Once you ride in it, it carries all living beings beyond sorrow. This vehicle is like space. It is a great palace that cannot be measured. It is the highest vehicle that brings clear joy, happiness, and bliss.

Whoever rides in it cannot be found going in any direction. They are taught to go to peace beyond sorrow, but no going is found. Think of a dead person who has nowhere to go. For this reason, that person is completely called peace beyond sorrow.

You cannot find the awakening hero in the earlier limit, the later end, or the present. The past, present and future are pure. That awakening hero is not made by causes and is free from tangled thinking. This is the practice of the highest perfect wisdom.

A wise and knowing awakening hero thinks about what is never born. They practice in this way. They develop great compassion without the idea of living beings. This is the practice of the highest perfect wisdom.

You do not hold onto form or feeling. You do not hold onto an idea or an intention. You do not hold onto awareness. By not holding onto these, you stay in the true nature of things. This is how you practice supreme perfect wisdom.

You do not hold onto what is lasting or always changing. You do not hold onto happiness or suffering, or what is nice or not nice. You do not hold onto a self or no self. You do not hold onto the way things really are, or emptiness. You do not hold onto getting the fruit. You do not hold onto the level of a worthy one. You do not hold onto the level of a solitary Buddha, or even the level of a Buddha.

The Guide does not stay in the realm not made by causes. He also does not stay in things made by causes. He practices by not staying anywhere. In the same way, an awakening hero rests on a base through a stay without staying. The Victorious One taught that a stay without staying is the true way to stay.

Some people wish to be a listener of the Well-Gone One. Others wish to become a solitary Buddha. Some wish to be a King of the Teaching, a Buddha. But they cannot reach these goals without relying on this patience. It is like trying to cross a river without finding a way to the other shore.

Think of the teaching, the listening, and what is taught. Think of getting the fruit. Think of the solitary Buddha and the Protector of the World. Think of the peace beyond sorrow reached by wise and clear minds. The Thus-Gone One taught that all these things are like an illusion.

Four kinds of persons are not afraid of this. The first is a child of the Victorious Ones who is skilled in the truth. The second is someone who is never turning back. The third is a worthy one who has washed away dirt and dropped all doubt. The fourth is someone fully held by a wise friend.

Wise people act with benefit and compassion. They train in these words of knowing and touch awakening. There is happiness made by causes and happiness not made by causes. You should know that all that happiness comes from this.

Seeds planted in the earth will sprout. When the right conditions come together, many different shapes are born. The five perfections and all the good qualities of awakening are the same. All of them are born from perfect wisdom.

A ruler of the whole world travels along a path. The seven treasures and all his armies follow on that very path. Wherever the perfect wisdom of the Victorious Ones goes, it is the same. All the good qualities will follow right along that path.

The Victorious One asked Shakra a question, and Shakra answered. "Imagine Buddha-lands as many as the grains of sand in the Ganges river. Imagine they were all filled to the top with the relics of the Victorious Ones. Even then, I would take this perfect wisdom."

Why? It is not that I lack respect for the relics. But they are worshipped because they are filled with wisdom. A person gets respect by relying on a king. In the same way, the relics of a Buddha rely on perfect wisdom.

A precious jewel has every good quality and is priceless. Whatever box it rests in deserves respect. Even if the jewel is taken out, people still take joy in the box. This is because those good qualities belong to that precious jewel.

A wise and smart awakening hero practices like this. They do not train in the level of a worthy one. They do not train in the level of a solitary Buddha. For the sake of knowing everything, they train following a Buddha's qualities. Whoever does not train in learning and not learning, that is real training.

They do not train to make form grow or shrink. They do not train to hold onto form. They do not train to hold onto different things. Still, they train and fully hold onto knowing everything. This sure way out is the training of those who love good qualities.

Form is not wisdom. There is no wisdom in form. Awareness, an idea, feeling, and intention are not wisdom. There is no wisdom in them, either. This is exactly like the element of space. There is no difference at all.

The nature of something to hold onto is boundless. Whatever the nature of living beings is, that is also boundless. The nature of the element of space is also boundless. The wisdom of the Knower of the World is boundless, too.

The Guide has clearly taught that an idea is this shore. By breaking down and leaving behind every idea, you cross to the far shore. Those who become free from any idea reach the far shore. They stay in the word of the Teacher.

The Teacher could stay for as many ages as there are grains of sand. He could clearly say the words 'living beings.' But since they are pure from the very start, how could living beings ever arise? This is the practice of the highest perfection, perfect wisdom.

When I spoke the truth of this highest perfection, the highest being of the past spoke to me. He said, 'In the future, you will become a Buddha.' I received this prediction. This is what the Victorious One said.

The Protectors practice this perfect wisdom. If you respect it, remember it, and understand what it means, you will be safe. Poison, weapons, fire, and water will not hurt you. Mara and Mara's side will find no chance against you.

Imagine someone builds shrines out of the seven treasures. They build them for a Well-Gone One who has passed into the final peace beyond sorrow. They make offerings there. Imagine they build as many shrines as there are grains of sand in the Ganges river. Imagine these shrines fill thousands of millions of lands.

Imagine all the living beings in those endless millions of lands do no other work. Instead, they make offerings for an age or longer. They offer heavenly flowers, sweet incense, and oils in the past, present and future.

The ten powers of the Guides will come from this wisdom. So, someone might write this Mother of the Well-Gone Ones in a book. They might keep it and honor it with flowers and sweet oils. If they do, they gain much more stored-up goodness. Building and making offerings to all those shrines does not even match a tiny part of it.

This perfect wisdom of the Victorious Ones is a great spell of knowledge. It calms the sorrow and suffering in the many realms of living beings. The Protectors of the World lived in the past and live now in the ten directions. They all trained in these words of knowing. By doing this, they became the greatest kings of healers.

Whoever does not get stuck on form does not get stuck on feeling. They do not get stuck on any idea or intention. Whoever does not get stuck on awareness rests in the true nature of things. This is the practice of perfect wisdom, the highest perfection.

In the same way, supreme perfect wisdom has great good qualities. Because of these, even after the Victorious Ones pass into the peace beyond sorrow, people worship their relics. Therefore, anyone who wants to hold the good qualities of the Victorious Ones should take up this perfect wisdom. This is freedom.

Wisdom comes before giving generosity. It also comes before good conduct, patience, steady effort, and deep focus. Wisdom holds them all together so that these qualities of goodness are not wasted. This shows that all things share a single way.

For example, there are billions of trees in Jambudvipa. They have many different forms and kinds. We might talk about counting their many shadows. But the shadows themselves are not really different from one another.

In the same way, the five perfections of the Victorious Ones get the very name of perfect wisdom. You can dedicate them for the sake of knowing everything. When you do, all six perfections share one taste. This one taste is called awakening.

An awakening hero might not fully understand. They might teach that form, idea, feeling, intention, and awareness are always changing. But if they do, they act on a made-up idea. Wise people never destroy things.

You do not see anything as form or feeling. You do not find any idea. You do not hold onto awareness. You do not find any intention. Instead, you fully know that all things are never born and are empty. This is how you practice supreme perfect wisdom.

The Protectors practice this perfect wisdom. This perfection keeps people safe. If anyone respects, remembers, and truly understands it, they will not be hurt by poison, weapons, fire, or water. Mara and Mara's side will never find a chance to harm them.

The perfect wisdom of the Victorious Ones is a great spell of knowledge. These words of knowing calm the sadness and suffering in every realm of living beings. Every Protector of the World from the past and in the ten directions trained in this perfection. By learning it, each became a perfect doctor and an unsurpassed king of healers.

Whenever a ruler of the whole world travels, the seven treasures and his army follow his path. Wherever the perfect wisdom of a Victorious One goes, every good quality also travels along that path. All these qualities follow this perfection of wisdom.

A Victorious One asked Shakra a question, and Shakra replied. He said, 'Imagine there were as many Buddha-lands as grains of sand in the Ganges river. Even if they were all completely filled with the relics of Victorious Ones, I would still choose this perfect wisdom. I would take this very perfection of wisdom.'

If you ask why, it is not because I lack respect for a relic. People honor these relics because they are filled with wisdom. Think of a person who serves a king. People show them respect because they rely on the king. In the same way, a relic of a Buddha is respected because it relies on perfect wisdom. It relies on this perfection of wisdom.

Supreme perfect wisdom has great good qualities. Because of this perfection, the relics of the Victorious Ones are honored even after they pass into the peace beyond sorrow. Anyone who wants to hold the good qualities of the Victorious Ones should take up this perfect wisdom. This is freedom.

In this practice, you do not take anything as form or feeling. You do not find any idea. You do not take anything as awareness. You do not find any intention. You fully know that all things are never born and are empty. This is the practice of supreme perfect wisdom. It is the highest perfection.

You might know that these things stop and fade away. The goal you dedicate them to fades away too. One of these things never dedicates to another of these things. If you understand this perfectly, then you truly dedicate.

If you make a sign out of your action, you do not really dedicate. But if there are no signs, this is the true dedication to awakening. Imagine eating delicious food mixed with poison. The Victorious One teaches that treating good things as something to hold onto is just like that poison.

So, you should practice how to dedicate like this. The Victorious Ones fully know goodness. They know every way it appears, where it comes from, and its defining feature. You must rejoice in that goodness. Then you dedicate it in exactly the same way.

If you dedicate stored-up goodness to awakening like this, it has no poison. You stay close to the Buddha. You speak exactly what the Victorious One has said. A hero who dedicates in this way shines very bright. They outshine every awakening hero in the world who is one who holds onto something.

Imagine millions of blind people with no guide. They do not even know the path. How could they ever find the city? Without wisdom, these five perfections have no eyes. Because they have no guide, they cannot reach awakening.

But when these practices are perfectly guided by wisdom, they gain eyes. Then they finally earn the name of perfections. Think of a beautiful painting that is missing its eyes. The artist earns no payment until the eyes are painted on.

Imagine someone helps all living beings in lands as many as the grains of sand in the Ganges river. They help everyone become a worthy one. Now, imagine someone else writes down this perfect wisdom. Then they give the text to a great living being. This second person gets much more stored-up goodness.

Why is that? The best speakers train in this. They show that all things are emptiness. When a listener hears this, they quickly reach freedom. This is how someone reaches the awakening of a solitary Buddha and a Buddha's awakening.

Without a little sprout, a tree never grows in the world. How could branches, leaves, flowers, and fruits ever grow on it? It is the same without the wish to awaken. Without it, a Victorious One never appears in the world. How then could Shakra, Brahma, and the listener ever appear?

When the sun shines its web of light, living beings do their work. It is the same for the wise. They give rise to the wish to awaken in the world to truly know. Through deep knowing, living beings gain good qualities.

Think about Lake Anavatapta. If the lord of the serpent spirits did not live there, how could rivers flow here in Jambudvipa? If there were no rivers, no flowers or fruits could grow. Without rivers, the ocean would not have many forms of jewels.

It is the same here. Without the wish to awaken, how could the deep knowing of the Well-Gone One appear in all these worlds? Without deep knowing, good qualities do not grow, and there is no awakening. Then a Buddha's qualities, which are like a great ocean, would not exist.

Think of all the glowing creatures in this world. Imagine all the light they shine together. A single ray of light from the sun is far better. All the light from those creatures cannot match even a tiny part of the sun's light.

All the listeners might gather a huge pile of stored-up goodness. They build this through generosity, good conduct, and meditation. But an awakening hero only needs a single thought to rejoice. The stored-up goodness of all those listeners cannot match a tiny part of the awakening hero's rejoicing.

Think of the billions of Buddhas from the past. Think of those living right now in endless millions of lands. Think of all the Protectors of the world who have passed into the peace beyond sorrow. They all share the jewel teaching to end suffering.

Think of the time from when they first made the wish for highest awakening. Think all the way to when the true teaching of those Guides comes to an end. During all that time, those Victorious Ones gather stored-up goodness. Think of all that stored-up goodness, everything that has the perfections, and a Buddha's qualities.

Think of the time from when they first make the wish for highest awakening until the true teaching of those Guides comes to an end. Think of all the stored-up goodness those Victorious Ones have during that time. Think of everything that is filled with the perfections and a Buddha's qualities.

Sharing this perfection of wisdom is much better.
