If a wise awakening hero, skilled in clever ways, rejoices in a good deed that stores up goodness and dedicates this stored-up goodness to the highest awakening for the sake of living beings, they outshine all beings by dedicating it.

There are many diseases and harmful spirits in the human world. People with compassion calm them through a blessing of truth. Even so, these helpers feel no self-importance and do not give rise to pride. You should know they have a prediction of never turning back.

But someone might perform a blessing of truth and feel self-importance, thinking, "I have a prediction." Or they might feel self-importance because other awakening heroes made a prediction about them. You should know that anyone who stays stuck in self-importance has little understanding.

Sometimes Mara approaches someone and tries to trick them using names. He says, "These are the names of you and your parents. These are the names of your family going back seven generations. And when you become a Buddha, this will be your name."

Mara tells them about the strict practices and training they will do. He says, "Your past good qualities and actions were just like this, too." If any awakening hero hears these words and feels self-importance, Mara has completely tricked them. You should know they have little understanding.

An awakening hero might live far away in lonely villages, cities, or mountain valleys. They might stay in a deep forest or a quiet woodland retreat. But if they praise themselves and put down others, Mara has completely tricked them. You should know they have little understanding.

A true hero might always live among people in villages, provinces, and towns. They only work hard for awakening and for helping living beings grow. They do not wish to become a worthy one or a solitary Buddha. This way of living is taught as the quiet aloneness of a son of the Well-Gone One.

If a tree has no sprout, it never grows in the world. Then how could branches, leaves, flowers, and fruit ever appear on it? It is the same without the wish to awaken. Without it, a Victorious One does not appear in the world. Then how could the fruits, like Shakra, Brahma, and the listeners, ever appear?

This teaching of the Guides is deep and hard to see. No one has realized it, and there is nothing to be reached. So, when the Kind Helper reached awakening, he paused. He thought, "Who among all the living beings will understand this?"

When doing their training, they do not cling to the training itself. They do not grasp at a learner or at the things to train in. They do not hold on to the ideas of training or not training. Anyone who practices like this is training in a Buddha's qualities.

The defining feature of perfect wisdom is being empty. You should know that the defining feature of all these things is just like that. You must see clearly that things are empty and without signs. Practicing in this way is the wisdom practice of the Well-Gone Ones.

Living beings have many thoughts and desire food. Those whose minds cling to the cycle of rebirth wander forever. Both the self and the things of a self are not real and are empty. Yet the unwise act as if they are tying knots in the sky.

For example, someone might have the idea that they drank poison. They will faint even if no poison actually entered their body. The unwise act just like this. They insist on a self and what belongs to self. Because of this untrue idea of a self, they keep being born and dying in an always changing world.

Wherever there is clinging, complete mental trouble is taught. When you do not find a self and what belongs to self, this is called becoming completely clean. Truly, there is no thing that gets mental trouble or becomes pure. When an awakening hero understands this, they realize perfect wisdom.

Think of all the living beings in Jambudvipa without exception. Imagine if all of them were to form the wish for highest awakening. They might practice generosity for millions of years. They could dedicate all of this as a cause of awakening to help all beings.

Now imagine someone who works hard at the highest perfect wisdom. They might follow it for just a single day. All of that generosity cannot match even a tiny piece of this person's stored-up goodness. Because of this, you should always practice wisdom without being lazy.

A meditator practices the highest perfect wisdom. They feel great compassion, but they do not hold onto the idea of living beings. Because of this, the wise meditator becomes a worthy recipient for all beings. Whenever they eat the alms given by the world, it is truly meaningful.

An awakening hero might want to set free the living beings in the god and human worlds and the three lower realms. They want to show all living beings the wide path to the other shore. To do this, they must try hard day and night in perfect wisdom.

Imagine someone finds the highest jewel after never having one before. They might get so happy that they become careless right away and lose it. Because it is lost, they feel constant suffering as they wish for their jewel back.

In the same way, someone who has entered the highest awakening must not give up their training in perfect wisdom. Perfect wisdom is like a jewel. Think of a person who finds a jewel, wraps it up carefully, and travels quickly on their way until they reach peace.

Think of the bright sun rising in a sky without clouds. Its rays completely destroy the thick, dark night. As it shines, it outshines all the little fireflies and living creatures. It even outshines all the stars and the bright light of the moon.

In the same way, an awakening hero practices the highest perfect wisdom. They practice emptiness and act without signs. By doing this, the wise hero destroys the thick darkness of wrong view. They outshine all beings, worthy ones, solitary Buddhas, and many other awakening heroes.

Someone might sit in a mountain cave five hundred leagues wide. They might sit with snakes for millions of years. But an awakening hero must understand true quiet aloneness. If they do not, they only end up feeling better than others. They stay mixed up in the world.

An awakening hero might work hard to help beings. They might gain deep focus, power, ability, freedom, and deep calm. Someone might look down on them and say, "This person does not practice in the quiet forest." The Victorious One says this proud person lives in Mara's domain.

A person might live in a busy village or in a forest. They might leave behind the goals of the two vehicles and aim only for the highest awakening. This is true quiet aloneness for those working for the good of beings. An awakening hero ruins their own path if they judge others.

Therefore, a wise person who seeks the highest awakening must be strong. They must completely destroy their pride. Think of sick people trying to get well. They must trust a doctor to cure them. In the same way, you must carefully trust a wise friend.

Buddhas and awakening heroes have entered the highest awakening. You should trust them and every perfection as a wise friend. They are the teachers, and this is the level of accomplishment. These are the two causes. Through them, a Buddha's awakening is quickly reached.

Think of every Victorious One in the past, the future, and the ten directions. This perfection is the only path for all of them. Are you stepping toward the highest awakening? Then this perfection is your brightness, your lamp, and your light. It is your greatest teacher.

Think of a prince who wants to give away his wealth. He becomes a great leader that everyone wants to meet. Even now, he brings joy to many living beings. Imagine how much more he will do when he learns clever ways and rules the kingdom!

In the same way, an awakening hero who is skilled in practicing wisdom gives the nectar of deathlessness. They bring joy to gods and humans. Even now, they work hard to help many living beings. Imagine how much more they will do when they become a King of the Teaching!

At that time, Mara hurts as if poked by a thorn. He is full of sadness, suffering, worry, and weakness. He thinks, "How can I make this awakening hero give up?" He sets the sky on fire and throws shooting stars to scare them.

When these wise ones are truly determined, they see the high meaning of perfect wisdom day and night. Then their body, mind, and speech move as freely as a bird in the sky. How could any helper of the Dark One find a chance to stop them?

When awakening heroes fight and argue, they stay mad and do not get along. At that time, Mara rejoices and becomes very happy. He thinks, "Those two will wander far away from the deep knowing of the Victorious Ones."

Those two will wander far away and act like flesh-eating monsters. They will both break their own promises. How can there be awakening for those who are mean and lack patience? At that time, the Maras and their followers will rejoice.

If there is no sprout, a tree could never grow in the world. Without a tree, how could branches, leaves, flowers, and fruit ever appear? In the same way, without the wish to awaken, a Victorious One would never appear in the world. Without a Victorious One, how could the fruits—like Shakra, Brahma, and listeners—ever appear?

For example, when the life force stops, all other abilities stop too, no matter how many there are. In the same way, for the great wise ones who practice wisdom, all the perfections are gathered into this one.

Wise awakening heroes train in all the good qualities that listeners have. They also train in all the good qualities of the solitary Buddhas. But they do not stay stuck in these qualities or want them for themselves. They just think, "This is what I must train in," and so they train.

Some people fully enter into the highest awakening with no turning back. If you rejoice deep in your heart when they are making the wish to awaken, you create great goodness. You could measure the huge Mount Meru of this vast system of worlds by weighing it on a scale, but you cannot weigh the goodness when you rejoice like that.

There are many living beings who look for goodness and want to help others. You should also rejoice in the heap of stored-up goodness of them all. Because of this, when they gain the good qualities of the Victorious Ones, they will give the gift of teaching to the world to end suffering.

An awakening hero is without made-up thoughts and fully knows that all things are empty, without signs, and free from tangled thinking. This awakening hero does not look for awakening using a wisdom that splits things in two. Instead, that meditator works hard at the highest perfect wisdom.

The element of space and anything that goes against that space do not exist, and no one has ever caught it. In the same way, the awakening hero who is skilled in the practice of wisdom is just like space, and practices complete peace.

Imagine an awakening hero who has not received a prediction. If they get angry and fight with someone who has a prediction, they have bad thoughts. For every single angry moment, they must put on their armor from the very beginning. They will have to start over for that many ages.

A Buddha reaches awakening through the perfection of patience. Learners use careful attention and think, "This mind is not good." They own up to their mistakes. They promise to stop themselves next time. They do not enjoy bad thoughts. This is how they train in a Buddha's qualities.

When they practice, they do not hold onto any training at all. They do not hold onto a learner or the things to train in. They do not think about training and not training. A person who practices like this trains in a Buddha's qualities.

An awakening hero who understands this training will never ruin it. They will never lose their good conduct. They practice this to gain a Buddha's qualities. They are highly skilled at the higher training. They know there is nothing to hold onto.

They practice the wisdom of the wise light-makers in this way. They do not create even a single thought that is not good. Think of the sun moving high up in the sky. Its bright rays completely wipe out the shadows. Darkness cannot stay in the empty space before it.

For those who have trained in perfect wisdom, every other perfection is included right here. The mistaken view of a self contains all the sixty-two views. In the exact same way, it is taught that every perfection is included right inside this wisdom.

Imagine a person made by magic standing in a crowd. This person does not think, "I must make these people happy." But they still do! They might show off many magic powers. Yet they have no body, no mind, and not even a name.

It is the same for those who practice wisdom. They never think, "After I reach awakening, I will free all beings." They take on different kinds of birth and do many things. They show these actions like an illusion, but they practice without fixed ideas.

Think of a magic copy of a Buddha. It does a Buddha's deed without feeling any pride at all. In the same way, an awakening hero who is skilled in practicing wisdom acts just like a magic creation and an illusion.

A clever woodworker can make wooden figures of men and women. These figures can do all kinds of work. In the same way, an awakening hero who is skilled in practicing wisdom does everything through deep knowing free of thoughts.

When someone practices so well, a great crowd of gods will put palms together. They bow down and show respect. All the Buddhas in the world systems of the ten directions sing praises for their good qualities.

Think of all the living beings in worlds as countless as the sands of the Ganges. If they all became Maras, and made even more Maras from every hair on their bodies, they still could not create obstacles for the wise.

A wise awakening hero is strong because of four causes. Because of these, the four Maras cannot defeat or shake them. First, they rest in emptiness. Second, they do not leave living beings behind. Third, they do exactly as they say. Fourth, they have the blessing of the Well-Gone Ones.

Perfect wisdom is the Mother of the Thus-Gone Ones. When it is taught, an awakening hero might wish to learn it. They might work hard to practice it with a true heart. You should know this noble person has stepped into knowing everything.

They do not rest in the expanse of all things or the way things really are. Instead, they rest without resting, like a cloud in the sky. Think of a holder of magic words traveling in the sky without a home. If they wish to stay somewhere, they use their words of power. They can make flowers bloom out of season and bless the place just as they wish.

Practicing like this, the wise and bright awakening hero does not grasp at the mind that understands. They do not grasp at a Buddha's qualities. They do not grasp at a teacher, a person who wants the teaching, or someone holding a view. This is how people rest when they want peace and delight in every good quality.

Listeners and solitary Buddhas rest in deep calm. Their rest is deeply peaceful and full of joy, no matter how many there are. But this way of resting is the highest and best of them all. It is second only to the freedom of the worthy ones and the Thus-Gone Ones.

Birds live in the sky, but they do not fall. Fish live in the water, but they do not drown and die. In the same way, the awakening hero uses the power of deep focus. They reach the far shore and rest in emptiness. Still, they do not pass into peace beyond sorrow.

Think of an illusion, like a person made by magic standing in a crowd. They do not think, "I must please these people," but they still do it. You can see them showing off different magic powers. Even so, they have no body, no mind, and not even a name.

There are many kinds of deep knowing, gateways, clever ways, and roots. All of these come from supreme perfect wisdom. When helping causes come together, the machine of deeds appears. Yet perfect wisdom never runs out and never grows.

An awakening hero uses this wisdom to understand arising from causes together. They know it is never born and never runs out. A sun with no clouds shines light to chase away the dark. In the same way, the hero destroys thick ignorance and reaches the state that is arisen by itself.

These heroes have great power. They rest in the four kinds of deep focus. Yet they do not rely on them, and they do not truly stay in them. Still, these four kinds of deep focus and their parts act as a support. They help the hero reach supreme, wonderful awakening.

They have supreme wisdom and rest in deep focus. They also feel the four wonderful kinds of formless deep calm. This deep focus helps them reach supreme, wonderful awakening. Yet the awakening hero does not train just to end their inner flaws.

This is a great wonder of those who gather good qualities. They rest in deep focus and deep calm. They see that these states are without signs. If their bodies die while they rest there, they are born again in the desire realm. They are born exactly where they wish to be.

Think of a person from Jambudvipa. They have never visited the supreme city of the gods in the realm of the gods. But later, they travel there. They see those places held by the gods. When they return here, they do not cling to them.

Someone might want to reach the highest good qualities of all living beings. They might want to touch a Buddha's deep knowing, which is amazing and supreme. They might wish to give the best and holy gift of teaching. That person should rely on this supreme home of the helpers.

When the Guides explain all the trainings, this training is the very best. It is higher than any other training. A wise person might want to reach the far shore of all trainings. They should practice this training in perfect wisdom. This is the training of the Buddhas.

This is the supreme treasure of teaching and the holy treasury of the teaching. It is the Buddha family. It is a treasury of happiness and joy for beings. The Protectors of the world live in the past, the future, and the ten directions. All of them come from this. Even so, the expanse of all things never runs out.

Think of all the trees, fruits, flowers, and forests. They all grow and come up from the earth. But the earth is never used up, and it never gets bigger. It does not shrink. It is without fixed ideas, and it never gets tired.

Think of the children of the Buddha, the listeners, the solitary Buddhas, and the gods. Think of all the happy and joyful things for beings. They all come from supreme perfect wisdom. Yet this wisdom never runs out, and it never grows larger.

There are many living beings, whether they are low, average, or great. The Well-Gone One taught that they all come from ignorance. When helping causes come together, the machine of suffering starts up. Yet that machine of ignorance never runs out and never grows larger.

Like this, awakening heroes hold the highest good qualities. They work hard in their training. They rest in deep calm and deep focus. Then they live in the desire realm again without being attached. Like a lotus growing in water, they do not live by the ways of the unwise.

Great heroes act only to bring living beings to maturity. They make the lands pure and finish the perfections. They think, 'The good qualities of awakening and the perfections would fade.' Because of this, they do not try to be born in the formless realm.

Imagine a person who finds a hidden treasure of jewels. At first, they do not feel any desire for the jewels. Later on, they decide to take the whole treasure. They take the jewels and go home, but they do not become attached to them.

In the same way, wise awakening heroes give joy and happiness. They reach four peaceful states of deep calm and deep focus. Then they let go of the happiness from that deep calm and deep focus. Filled with compassion for others, they enter the desire realm again.

Suppose an awakening hero rests in deep calm and deep focus. But they start to want the vehicle of a worthy one or a solitary Buddha. Then they are not settled in meditation. They become restless and have a wandering mind. A Buddha's good qualities fade away from them, just like a sailor whose boat is wrecked.

Think about form, sound, smell, taste, and touch. These are the five pleasures of the senses. A hero might fully enjoy them. Yet they stay away from the vehicle of a worthy one or a solitary Buddha. Instead, they find joy in the wish to awaken. You should know this hero is always in steady stillness.

The pure awakening hero acts with the perfection of steady effort to help other living beings and persons. Think of a servant woman who draws water. She is completely under her master's power. In the same way, the heroes work under the power of all living beings.
Even if her master scolds or beats her, the servant woman does not say a word back. She thinks, 'He might even kill me.' She is deeply terrified and completely overcome with fear.

In the same way, those who seek highest awakening for the sake of awakening should act like servants to all beings. This is how awakening is reached and good qualities are perfected. It is like a fire that starts from grass and wood. That same fire then burns up the grass and wood.

Let go of your own happiness and do not expect anything in return. Work hard day and night for what other living beings need. Care for them from the bottom of your heart, without ever getting tired. Do this just like a mother caring for her only child.

An awakening hero might wish to stay in the cycle of rebirth for a long time. Such a meditator works hard to help living beings and for the cleansing of the land. If they do not feel even a tiny speck of weariness, they have the perfection of steady effort and are never careless.

An unwise awakening hero counts tens of millions of ages. They think the path to awakening is long and full of suffering. While trying to practice the true teaching, they will feel suffering for a long time. Because of this, their perfection of steady effort shrinks, and they become lazy.

An awakening hero has the excellent teaching of patience. Someone else might fill a vast system of worlds with jewels. They might offer these jewels to the Buddhas, the Knowers of the World, and to worthy ones and solitary Buddhas. But all that generosity cannot match even a tiny part of the patient hero's stored-up goodness.

The body of someone who rests in patience becomes completely pure. They have the thirty-two marks, endless power, and great strength. They share the highest teaching of emptiness with living beings. Wandering beings will rejoice in this wise person who has patience.

Some living beings might take a packet of sandalwood. They might rub it on the awakening hero with great respect. Someone else might throw burning coals on the hero's head. The awakening hero should keep an equal and even mind toward both of them.

The wise awakening hero practices patience in this way. They might dedicate their making the wish to awaken toward the highest awakening. By showing patience to the whole world, this hero outshines the worthy ones and solitary Buddhas. They outshine however many there are in the realm of living beings.

The person who practices patience should also think like this. "There is much suffering in hell, among animals, and in the world of Yama. I have helplessly felt harm caused by the pleasures of the senses. Why should I not practice patience now for the sake of awakening?"

"People might use whips, sticks, and weapons. They might beat me, tie me up, or even kill me. They might cut off my head, ears, hands, feet, and nose. I will bear with patience whatever sufferings there are in the world!" Thinking this, the awakening hero rests in the perfection of patience.

They form the wish for highest awakening. Then they wait to reach the awakening that nothing surpasses. If they feel all this time is just a single day and night, they are clear-minded and wise. You should know they have begun their steady effort.

Someone might say to them, 'You will reach highest awakening after you break down Mount Meru.' They might feel tired in their mind and worry about the mountain's size. If so, that awakening hero has become lazy.

But they might think, 'What is so hard about an amount like this?' They might decide to crush Mount Meru to dust in just one moment. That wise awakening hero has begun their steady effort. Before long, they will reach the highest awakening of a Guide.

They might think, 'I will fully ripen beings and act to help them.' They might work hard at this with their body, speech, and mind. But if they hold on to the idea of a self, they have actually become lazy. They become as far away from knowing everything as the sky is from the earth.

They might have no idea of a body, a mind, or living beings. They turn away completely from any idea, and they practice the teaching that is not two. The Benefactor has taught that this is the perfection of steady effort. It belongs to those who want the highest, peaceful, and endless awakening.

Others might speak badly and use harsh words. If a wise awakening hero hears this, they are glad and think, 'I am happy.' Who speaks? Who hears? By what is something said, what is said, and why? Since they have the highest perfection of patience, they are truly wise.

Through good conduct, those who want peace become noble. They stay in the space of the ten powers. Their good conduct is never broken. They follow every kind of self-control. They dedicate all of this to awakening to help all living beings.

If someone wants to reach the awakening of a worthy one or a solitary Buddha, they are lacking good conduct. They are foolish, and their actions fail. But they can dedicate their actions to the great peace of awakening instead. Then, even while enjoying a pleasure of the senses, they stay in the perfection of good conduct.

Some things surely make the good qualities of awakening grow. For those who have good qualities, this is the true goal of good conduct. Other things ruin the awakening of those who help others. The Guide has said that this is lacking good conduct.

An awakening hero might enjoy the five pleasures of the senses. But they have taken refuge in the Buddha, the teaching, and the noble community. They focus their mind on knowing everything and think, "I must become a Buddha." You should know that this wise person stays in the perfection of good conduct.

Someone might practice the ten paths of good action for ten million ages. But they might start to want the state of a worthy one or a solitary Buddha. Right then, their good conduct is broken and falls apart. Making the wish to awaken in that way is worse than a defeat.

They protect their good conduct and dedicate it to the highest awakening. They have no self-importance about it and do not praise themselves. They completely let go of the idea of a self and the idea of living beings. Such an awakening hero is said to stay in the perfection of good conduct.

An awakening hero might practice the path of the Victorious Ones and think, "These living beings are ones with good conduct, and these are lacking good conduct." By having these different ideas, they are entirely lacking good conduct. Their own good conduct breaks down, and they do not have pure good conduct.

Someone may have no idea of a self and no idea of living beings. If they are free from any idea and from wanting, how could they be not holding back? They have no self-importance about their self-control or their lack of self-control. The Guide taught that this is the good conduct of self-control.

Any pure living being who is one with good conduct does not focus on pleasant or unpleasant things. If they give away their head, hands, and feet, they do not have a discouraged mind. When they give away everything they own, they are always free from holding on.

They know the nature of things is no self and not solid. If they give away even their own flesh without a discouraged mind, why even mention giving away outside objects? It is impossible for them to act with stinginess.

People with the idea of a self become attached by thinking of things as mine. How could fools ever want to give? Stingy ones will be born in the realm of hungry ghosts. Even if they are born as humans, they will then be very poor.

The awakening hero knows that living beings are very poor. So the hero focuses on giving and always gives freely. To them, the beautiful four continents are just like a glob of spit. Giving them away brings great joy, but getting the four continents does not.

This teaching of the Guides is deep and hard to see. No one has realized it, and no one has reached it. So, when the Kind Helper reached awakening, he paused. He thought, "Who among all the living beings will understand this?"

The wise and bright awakening hero thinks of all the living beings in the three realms of existence. They think, "May this generosity be given to them!" They practice this generosity. Then they dedicate it to the highest awakening for the sake of all beings.

After giving generosity, they do not hold on to things. They never hope for a reward or a result that ripens. Because they are so skilled at giving, they give everything away. Even if they give just a little, it grows to become huge and endless.

Imagine every single one of the living beings in the three kinds of life. Imagine if all of them gave gifts for endless ages. Imagine they gave these gifts to the Knowers of the World, the Buddhas, the worthy ones, and the solitary Buddhas, while seeking to be a listener.

Now imagine a wise awakening hero who is skilled in clever ways. They rejoice in that good deed that stores up goodness. They dedicate this stored-up goodness to the highest awakening to help living beings. By dedicating it, they shine brighter than all those beings!

Even a huge pile of glass jewels is completely outshone by a single precious lapis lazuli. It is the same for all beings and their vast heap of generosity. They are all outshone by the awakening hero who knows how to rejoice.

Suppose an awakening hero gives gifts to beings. They do not claim the good result as "mine." They give away the object without holding back. Because of this, their root of goodness will grow with great power. It grows like the bright, cloudless moon getting fuller in the sky.
Teaching the step-by-step path.

This is the sixth topic: teaching the step-by-step path. An awakening hero's generosity stops life as a hungry ghost. It stops poverty and all mental trouble. While practicing this, they gain endless wealth. Through generosity, they help to fully mature living beings who are in suffering.

Through good conduct, they avoid many forms of life as an animal. They leave behind the eight unfree states. This way, they always find the freedom to practice. Through patience, they gain a great and wonderful body. They become golden and beautiful. They are a wonderful sight for others to see.

With steady effort, their qualities of goodness will not fade away. They will find the treasury of the Victorious Ones, which is endless deep knowing. With deep focus, they leave behind the bad qualities of worldly desire. They perfectly achieve knowledge, special knowings, and deep calm.

Through wisdom, they fully understand the nature of things. They will completely go beyond all the three realms. Then, as the Supreme Leader of People, they turn the precious wheel. They give the teaching to beings to bring an end to suffering.
Teaching full awakening in one moment.
Chapter seven teaches about full awakening in one moment. That awakening hero perfectly finishes all these things.
Teaching About the Teaching Body

Chapter eight teaches about the teaching body. The hero fully supports a perfectly pure land and pure living beings. They fully support the line of Buddhas and the line of the teaching. They also fully support the lineage of the community and all things.

The Best Healer cures the sickness of wandering beings. He gave this teaching on wisdom, which holds the path to awakening. This teaching is called the Collection of Precious Qualities, the path to awakening. He explained this path so that all living beings can reach it.
The Noble Verse Summary of Perfect Wisdom is complete.
